profile.headline: Spacecraft Flight Software
profile.jobTitle: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Spacecraft Flight Software

positions.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Spacecraft Flight Software
positions.description:
•	I am working on the Restore-L, Psyche, and TEMPO missions.
•	Restore-L is a satellite capable of refueling other satellites while in orbit.  Restore-L will launch in 2021 and will rendezvous with Landsat 7.
•	 Psyche is a probe that will explore and categorize the Psyche asteroid.  Psyche will launch in 2022 and rendezvous in 2025.
•	TEMPO is a hosted payload on a private satellite that will map and monitor pollution in North America.
•	For Restore-L, I am implementing Linux kernel and user space software which responds to time-sensitive S- and Ka-band transmissions. 
•	For Psyche, I am working with the PREEMPT_RT patch on top of the mainline Linux kernel to achieve consistent <30us response times at >10,000 interrupts per second.
•	For TEMPO, I am driving the integration requirements to accommodate the hosted payload, including the inertial measurement unit (SIRU), GPS receiver, telecommanding, and telemetry.
•	I implemented a library for Linux that allows Green Hills Integrity real-time application code to be linked and executed natively on Linux.  It is used on all three of my projects and many others.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Storage Management Group
•	Implemented high-performance real-time packet sniffing software to call out NFS clients causing volume access problems across the storage network.  This is a product sold by NetApp and deployed in customer environments.
•	Debugged DPDK user space technology to read packets from ethernet switch SPAN ports.

Platform Software Group, Analytics Group
•	The Mars team built a special-purpose operating system in user space based on the Debian distribution designed to maximize the benefits of all-flash storage devices.
•	Designed and implemented cross-board communication mechanism between the service processor and host operating system (Linux), both user space and kernel.  Without this, customers could not manage their storage when stuck in BIOS or Linux.
•	Improved uptime and error recovery by designing and implementing a mechanism for pushing DMAR errors from the Linux kernel to user space.

Platform Software Group, Core Infrastructure Group
•	Designed, implemented, and lead a team of engineers on an abstracted cross-component state aggregation and correlation software framework.  Prior to implementation, obtained formal approval from dozens of technical directors and senior engineers.  This product is sold by NetApp.
•	Determined that the support staff very often misconfigured SAS storage, necessitating a SAS error aggregation and correlation reference program utilizing the above framework, which plainly calls out SAS misconfigurations.
•	Designed and implemented a mathematical expression parser enabling dynamic update of error aggregation and correlation rules, increasing uptime by allowing error condition definition files to be applied and updated in real time without reboot.
•	Designed and coded multiple kernel modules, user applications, and daemons for a PowerPC 405GP embedded system under MontaVista Linux.  Proprietary serial-based communication system between system and host.  ECC kernel driver.  Serial-Ethernet software bridge for GDB.

positions.title: Senior Engineer
positions.description:
•	Designed and implemented kernel level virtualized file system calls presenting a consistent view to guest user applications across various Windows install types (known as the F Windows problem).  This became the foundation for the company’s next generation product.
•	Designed and implemented kernel level virtualized registry system calls.  Blended host and guest registry keys and values to form a consistent view for user applications across wildly differing hosts.  Virtualized registry symlinks and hive loads/unloads/imports/exports.
•	Engineered a safe driver unload mechanism considering delayed thread execution within kernel system calls, kernel resources, inline kernel patches, and asynchronous kernel callbacks.
•	Developed and released a Windows Vista beta product offering.
•	Worked closely with Adobe engineers to virtualize their LiveCycle ES document management product.  Resulted in the largest purchase order in company history.
•	Constructed an automated bug server to parse crash reports submitted by customers.  Automatically filed bugs in Bugzilla as necessary.
